claim: The schema-adequacy finding extends to operations, not just binding. The plan schema needs a transform slot with a bounded vocabulary to express 'apply operation X to a prior step output'. Free-form transform names are not resolvable by the executor.

design.tasks: 8 filesystem transform tasks (uppercase, lowercase, reverse, strip, len, words_sorted, composed uppercase+reverse, replace_spaces)

conditions.C_transform_list: deferral + transform slot with documented op list
conditions.D_transform_free: deferral + transform slot, no documented list

verdict_rule: PASS if bounded-list transform (C) closes the class (≥6/8) AND free-form transform (D) does not outperform C.
reading: String schema (A) fails 0/8 — the model invents pseudo-transform syntax the executor cannot resolve. Deferral alone (B) fails 0/8 — the model writes the raw value without applying the transform. Bounded-transform schema (C) closes 7/8. The bounded vocabulary is load-bearing: free-form transform names get invented (D) and are unresolvable. The one failure at C (t7, composed uppercase+reverse) is the compositional-transform boundary.

boundaries_found.compositional_transform: t7 (uppercase AND reverse) fails even with transform slot — requires list-form transform or pipeline representation. Next-session question.

artifacts.note: D_transform_free is partial — script crashed on the last item (parser, not model).
